text: In what year was the Equality Act passed?
explanation: The Equality Act was passed in 2010, consolidating and replacing a wide range of previous anti-discrimination legislation into a single Act.

text: What did the Equality Act 2010 do to previous anti-discrimination laws?

options.text: It added to them without changing anything
It consolidated and replaced a range of previous legislation — such as the Race Relations Act and Sex Discrimination Act — into one single Act
It only applied to public sector organisations
It transferred discrimination law to the EU

explanation: The Equality Act 2010 consolidated multiple previous anti-discrimination laws — including the Race Relations Act, Sex Discrimination Act and Disability Discrimination Act — into a single, simpler piece of legislation.

text: How many protected characteristics does the Equality Act cover?
explanation: The Equality Act covers 9 protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation.

text: Which of the following is NOT one of the 9 protected characteristics under the Equality Act?

options.text: Age
Disability
Wealth
Race

explanation: Wealth is not a protected characteristic. The 9 protected characteristics are: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation.

text: What is direct discrimination under the Equality Act?

options.text: Treating someone less favourably because of a protected characteristic
A policy that applies to everyone but disadvantages people with a protected characteristic
Failing to make reasonable adjustments for a disabled person
Making offensive comments about someone's religion

explanation: Direct discrimination is treating someone less favourably than others because of a protected characteristic — for example refusing to hire someone because of their age.

text: What is indirect discrimination under the Equality Act?

options.text: Treating someone worse because of who they are
A policy or practice that applies to everyone but puts people with a protected characteristic at a disadvantage
Refusing to make adjustments for a disabled employee
Verbal abuse directed at a colleague

explanation: Indirect discrimination occurs when a policy or practice applies to everyone but puts people with a protected characteristic at a particular disadvantage — for example requiring all staff to work Sundays may indirectly discriminate against some religious groups.

text: What is the duty to make reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act?

options.text: Employers must rebuild their workplace to accommodate any disability
Employers must make changes to remove disadvantages faced by disabled people — such as providing specialist equipment or adjusting working arrangements
All staff must complete diversity training annually
Employers must employ a minimum percentage of disabled workers

explanation: The duty to make reasonable adjustments requires employers to take steps to remove disadvantages faced by disabled people — such as providing adapted equipment, adjusting hours, or modifying duties.

text: How does the Equality Act apply to IT and software development?

options.text: It does not apply to the technology sector
IT systems and software must be accessible — discriminatory or inaccessible design could breach the Act
Only the recruitment process in IT companies is covered
Only hardware must comply, not software

explanation: IT systems and websites must be accessible to people with disabilities. Designing inaccessible systems or software that excludes people due to a protected characteristic could constitute a breach of the Equality Act.

text: What is harassment under the Equality Act?

options.text: Any form of criticism in the workplace
Unwanted conduct related to a protected characteristic that has the purpose or effect of violating dignity or creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive environment
Being passed over for promotion
Being asked to work overtime

explanation: Harassment is unwanted conduct related to a protected characteristic that violates a person's dignity or creates an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment.

text: What is victimisation under the Equality Act?

options.text: Being bullied by a manager
Being treated badly because you made or supported a complaint about discrimination
Being overlooked for a pay rise
Receiving a disciplinary warning

explanation: Victimisation means being treated badly because you made, or helped someone else make, a complaint about discrimination — protecting people from retaliation for raising equality concerns.

text: Which body enforces the Equality Act in Great Britain?

options.text: The Information Commissioner's Office
The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC)
The Health and Safety Executive
The Department for Work and Pensions

explanation: The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) enforces the Equality Act in Great Britain — it can conduct investigations and take legal action against organisations that breach equality law.

text: What is the public sector equality duty under the Equality Act?

options.text: Public sector organisations must employ equal numbers of men and women
Public bodies must have due regard to eliminating discrimination, advancing equality and fostering good relations between different groups
All public sector websites must be free to use
Public sector IT systems must be open source

explanation: The public sector equality duty requires public bodies to have due regard to: eliminating unlawful discrimination, advancing equality of opportunity, and fostering good relations between people with different protected characteristics.

text: A company's new HR software only works with a mouse and has no keyboard navigation. Why might this breach the Equality Act?

options.text: It doesn't — software is exempt from equality law
It may indirectly discriminate against employees with physical disabilities who cannot use a mouse
Only if the company employs more than 250 people
Only if the software was made by an overseas company

explanation: Software that is not accessible to people with physical disabilities may indirectly discriminate against them — the employer may also be failing in their duty to make reasonable adjustments.

text: Does the Equality Act cover job applicants as well as existing employees?

options.text: No — it only applies once someone is employed
Yes — discrimination in recruitment, selection and the terms offered is unlawful
Only for public sector roles
Only if the applicant has been shortlisted

explanation: The Equality Act covers the entire employment relationship including recruitment — discriminating against an applicant because of a protected characteristic during the hiring process is unlawful.

text: What is positive action under the Equality Act?

options.text: Mandatory quotas requiring a set percentage of women or minorities to be hired
Voluntary steps an employer can take to help people with protected characteristics who are disadvantaged or underrepresented
A legal requirement to promote people from minority groups first
Providing bonuses to employees from protected groups

explanation: Positive action allows employers to voluntarily take steps to help people with protected characteristics who are at a disadvantage or underrepresented — such as targeted training programmes. It is different from positive discrimination which is generally unlawful.
